name: Delaware
overview: Delaware collects delinquent county property taxes through the monition method in Title 9, Chapter 87 of the Delaware Code. The tax collecting authority files a praecipe with the prothonotary, a monition is posted on the property, and a writ commands the county sheriff to expose the real estate to public sale. The property itself is sold, and the sale goes to the Superior Court for approval. The owner may redeem within 60 days after the court approves the sale by paying the purchase price plus 15 percent and the costs of the case.

overview_sources.quote: The tax collecting authority may file a praecipe in the office of the prothonotary
We therefore now command you to expose to public sale, the real estate mentioned and described in said Monition as follows:
redeem the same at any time within 60 days from the day the sale thereof is approved by the Court
the amount of the purchase price and 15 percent in addition thereto

counties.office: Kent County Sheriff's Office (sale); Kent County Department of Finance, Division of Tax (procedures)
counties.schedule_rule: Monition Tax Sales take place January, April, July and October and are held on the last Tuesday of that month at 10:00 a.m.

sales.label: Monition (tax) sale
sales.deposit: $4,000 non-refundable cashier's check, certified check or money order per property, brought at registration (Sheriff's page, effective May 1, 2025). The county's Finance page still says $2,000; the Sheriff's page is the newer rule.
sales.registration_deadline: Registration ends at 9:45 a.m. on sale day
sales.note: Held at the Kent County Levy Court, 555 Bay Road, Dover, Chamber - Room 203. Balance due to the Sheriff's Office by 2:00 p.m. the same day (Finance page).
sales.quote: The next monition sale is scheduled for October 27th, 2026, at 10 am.

counties.next_sale_note: After October 27, 2026, no dated monition sale is posted yet; sales follow the quarterly rule (January, April, July, October).
counties.how_to_bid: Bid in person at the Kent County Levy Court in Dover. Register before 9:45 a.m. on sale day. The winning bidder pays a deposit for each property at the time of bidding and the balance to the Sheriff's Office by 2:00 p.m. the same day. The owner has 60 days from court confirmation to redeem; if the owner redeems, the bidder gets the price paid back plus 15%.
